tone.method: lexical cue counts on management sentences; indicative of wording, not a measure of business health

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: In the first quarter, we had solid performance across revenue and cash flow.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: These results are further proof of the quality of our portfolio and our hybrid cloud and AI strategy.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We had good performance in Software, at the high end of our model; continued strength in Infrastructure, above our model; while Consulting was below model.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: On a relative basis, Consulting outperformed the market.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Our cash flow generation is the strongest first quarter level we have reported in many years.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Before we get into more detail on the quarter, let me address the announcement of our agreement to acquire HashiCorp, a company we have partnered with for a long time and believe is a tremendous strategic fit with IBM.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Enterprise clients are wrestling with an unprecedented expansion in infrastructure applications across public and private cloud as well as on-prem environments, making this the ideal time to pursue this acquisition.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: As generative AI deployment accelerates alongside traditional workloads, developers are working with increasingly heterogeneous, dynamic, and complex infrastructure strategies.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: HashiCorp has a proven track record of helping clients manage the complexity of today's infrastructure by automating, orchestrating, and securing hybrid and multi-cloud environments.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: HashiCorp is a great strategic addition to our portfolio, extending Red Hat's hybrid cloud capabilities to provide end-to-end automated infrastructure and security lifecycle management.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: HashiCorp's technology is foundational to enabling the transition to hybrid and multi-cloud, and Terraform is the industry standard for infrastructure automation for these environments.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: With security top of mind for every enterprise, Vault is a powerful secrets management offering to automate identity security across applications.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: The combination will also bolster our leading IT automation platform to address the sprawling complexity of AI-driven application and infrastructure growth.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: HashiCorp's products have wide-scale adoption in the developer community, highlighting the pervasive nature of their technology used by over 85% of the Fortune 500 and downloaded over 0.5 billion times.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: The acquisition of HashiCorp builds on IBM's commitment to industry collaboration, the developer community, and open source hybrid cloud and AI innovation.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Today's acquisition is consistent with our M&A strategy.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We have taken a disciplined approach to M&A, and HashiCorp aligns well across all our key criteria to continue to focus and strengthen our portfolio on hybrid cloud and AI, deliver synergies with the rest of IBM, and be near-term accretive to free cash flow.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We have agreed to acquire HashiCorp for $6.4 billion in enterprise value to be funded by cash on hand.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: The transaction was approved by HashiCorp's Board of Directors.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Closing is anticipated by the end of 2024, subject to approval by HashiCorp's shareholders, regulatory approvals, and other customary closing conditions.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We have been executing a disciplined capital allocation strategy, and the acquisition of HashiCorp meets all of our criteria, including strategic fit, as Arvind just walked through, synergies across IBM, and financial accretion.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We see multiple drivers of product synergies within IBM and accelerating growth for HashiCorp.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Product synergies span across multiple strategic growth areas for IBM, including Red Hat, watsonx, data security, IT automation, and consulting.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: For example, the powerful combination of Red Hat's Ansible automation platform's configuration management and Terraform's automation will simplify provisioning and configuration of applications across hybrid cloud environments.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We are well positioned to drive growth for HashiCorp by leveraging IBM's enterprise incumbency and global reach.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: With 70% of the revenue today coming from the U.S., the opportunity to scale HashiCorp across IBM's operations in 175 countries is significant.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We also believe we can accelerate HashiCorp's adoption with IBM clients.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: To put this in perspective, only about 20% of the Forbes Global 2000 are HashiCorp customers and just 25% of HashiCorp customers result in more than $100,000 in annual recurring revenue, underscoring the opportunity to better monetize and upsell their products.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Bringing it all together, the acquisition allows us to deliver a more comprehensive hybrid cloud offering to enterprise clients, enhancing IBM's ability to capture global cloud opportunities.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Finally, we expect to realize operating efficiencies and expect the transaction to be accretive to adjusted EBITDA within the first full year post-close and to free cash flow in year two.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Significant near-term cost synergies underpin the financial profile of the transaction, while product synergies represent further upside.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We are very comfortable with our strong balance sheet, liquidity profile, and solid investment-grade rating and remain committed to our dividend policy.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We expect the global economy to behave similarly to last year, albeit with some uncertainty due to persistently high interest rates.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: AI-driven productivity, in particular, continues to be a top priority for businesses for both cost reductions and new revenue opportunities.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: I will now provide some details on the execution of our strategy around hybrid cloud and AI.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Enterprise AI continues to gain traction.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: This year, we anticipate more clients moving from experimenting to deploying AI at scale to unlock productivity.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We are pleased with the solid progress of our AI offerings.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Each quarter, we are winning more clients, expanding partnerships, and introducing new innovations.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Inception to date, our book of business related to watsonx and generative AI is greater than $1 billion with sequential quarter-over-quarter growth.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We believe our comprehensive AI strategy is well positioned to help clients scale AI.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We developed our watsonx platform for clients to build their AI solutions, spanning from foundation model training to data preparation and governance.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We have leveraged watsonx to build AI assistance through our software portfolio.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Our consultants are helping clients navigate the AI landscape.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: And finally, we are seeing our infrastructure segment play a larger role as clients leverage their hardware investments in their AI strategies.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: As AI becomes widely adopted, IBM Z is uniquely advantaged.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We believe a lot of AI inferencing will happen where the data is for security, efficiency, and latency reasons.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Our full-stack focus, from on-chip AI processing to AI accelerator cards, to watsonx platform support, allows models to be built and trained on any platform and easily deployed on IBM Z. The Telum chip is a unique differentiator, enabling real-time AI inferencing.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Generative AI is also driving lift for our storage offerings where industry-leading performance and scalability is utilized for data curation, model building, and fine-tuning.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: For enterprises to deploy AI at scale, AI is not a one-size-fits-all proposition.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: They appreciate having the ability to leverage a combination of AI models, whether they're IBM's, their own models, or open-source models, such as Llama from Meta and Mixtral from Mistral.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: And they can deploy these AI models across multiple environments.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: The flexibility we offer is resonating as our use cases are both large and more efficient models.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We are committed to an open innovation ecosystem around AI to help our clients maximize flexibility and leverage skills.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We see early parallels to Linux in making open-source AI models performant for enterprise use.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We believe that IBM with Red Hat can be a key driver of open-source AI.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: As you know, we have done a lot of work with AI models and recently released a family of state-of-the-art open-source code models from our Granite series.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Red Hat and IBM also recently launched Instruct Lab to evolve and improve AI models through incremental community contributions, much like open-source software.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: This open strategy is resonating around the world.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We recently announced a collaboration with the Spanish government to leverage IBM's investments across their entire AI stack and open source to build the world's leading suite of foundation models proficient in the Spanish language.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Enterprise use cases addressing code modernization, customer service, and digital labor remain top of mind for our clients.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: This quarter, we signed a multiyear contract with Providence Health to reimagine talent and HR workflows with AI from IBM and partners.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Our partner ecosystem remains essential to both AI and hybrid cloud growth.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: This quarter, we progressed strategic partnerships with a number of industry leaders.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Consulting joined forces with NVIDIA to accelerate clients' AI journeys.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: ServiceNow will embed watsonx AI capabilities into the ServiceNow platform to accelerate enterprise digital transformation.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We also expanded our relationship with Adobe around OpenShift and watsonx as it relates to the Adobe Experience Platform.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We continue to invest in emerging technology as well, bringing new innovations to the market.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Since we put the world's first Quantum system on the cloud in 2016, we have deployed over 80 Quantum systems, and our users have run over 3 trillion programs to date.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We just installed a Quantum System One at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: This is the first IBM Quantum system on a college campus anywhere in the world.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We closed the sale of The Weather Company in the first quarter and expect to close the announced acquisition of StreamSets and webMethods from Software AG by midyear.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Overall, we had a positive start to the year, which gives us confidence in our next quarter and full-year expectations.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Our revenue for the quarter was up 3% at constant currency.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We saw an impact to our top line performance from the closing of The Weather Company earlier than expected in the quarter.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Software grew by 6% with growth across Hybrid Platform & Solutions and Transaction Processing and continued strength in our recurring revenue base.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Consulting was up 2%, reflecting organic growth.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We continue to have solid signings performance and a trailing 12-month book-to-bill of over 1.15.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Infrastructure had strong performance, delivering growth across all of our hardware offerings.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Looking at our profit metrics, we expanded operating gross margin by 100 basis points and operating pretax margin by 130 basis points over last year, inclusive of about 100 basis point currency headwind to pretax margin.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: At the end of January, we closed on the divestiture of The Weather Company, generating a pretax gain of $241 million in the quarter.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Mitigating that benefit, we took charges of $374 million to address workforce rebalancing.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Operating pretax margin was up 50 basis points, excluding the year-over-year impacts of workforce rebalancing and divestiture dynamics.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We are pleased with this performance, in line with our guidance of roughly 50 basis points of operating pretax margin improvement in 2024.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Margin expansion was driven by our operating leverage, product mix, and ongoing productivity initiatives.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: This allows for continued investments to drive innovation, which you can see in our higher R&D expense.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: This puts us on track to deliver about $12 billion of free cash flow for the year, with the growth largely driven by adjusted EBITDA.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Since our acquisition of Red Hat, excluding 2021 when we spun off Kyndryl, our operating net income to free cash flow realization averaged 120%.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: And two, given the shift in our portfolio to a growing software business, deferred income also contributes to our realization.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: In terms of cash uses, we returned $1.5 billion to shareholders in the form of dividends.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Software revenue grew 6% with good performance across both Hybrid Platform & Solutions and Transaction Processing.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: As mentioned in January, the Software revenue growth drivers for the year include Red Hat growth, acquisitions, strong recurring revenue, and transaction processing.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Hybrid Platform & Solutions revenue was up 7%.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Red Hat revenue grew 9%, reflecting solid performance across the 3 key solutions: RHEL, OpenShift, and Ansible.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Annual bookings growth was again in the mid-teens, with OpenShift up over 40% this quarter and RHEL and Ansible each up double digits.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Beyond Red Hat, recent acquisitions contributed to the growth profile of Hybrid Platform & Solutions as did new innovation areas, including watsonx.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: The combination of Apptio, acquired mid-last year, and our IT automation portfolio has delivered strong results, unlocking the full benefits of a fin op solution for technology investments across hybrid cloud environments.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: In fact, just this quarter, we partnered with Microsoft to bring Apptio to Azure and we'll co-sell to our joint customers, and Microsoft has agreed to adopt Apptio's capabilities in parts of their organization.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Our ARR, after removing The Weather Company and security services, is now $13.9 billion, up over 8% since last year.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Transaction Processing, with its strong base of recurring revenue, delivered revenue growth of 4%.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Clients continue to value this portfolio of mission-critical software, supporting growing workloads on our hardware platforms.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: And there's an increasing interest in generative AI application modernization capabilities, like watsonx Code Assistant for Z. Software segment profit was up 80 basis points while absorbing both key investments in innovation and about 1 point of currency impact in the quarter.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Our Consulting revenue was up 2%.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We continue to see clients prioritizing large data and technology transformation projects focused on driving productivity with AI and analytics.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Solid demand for our offerings led to signings growth of 4%, our highest absolute first quarter signings in recent history, and our trailing 12-month book-to-bill ratio remains over 1.15.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Our overall backlog remains healthy, up 7% year-over-year, and backlog erosion levels remain stable.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: At the same time, we saw both a lengthening of backlog duration driven by large-scale digital transformations and a reduced level of revenue realization in the quarter as clients tightened discretionary spending.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Contributing to growth across the business this quarter, our strategic partnerships continue to make up over 40% of our Consulting revenue, with both AWS and Azure practices growing double digits.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Additionally, our Red Hat practice grew revenue double digits.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Expanding upon our partnerships, we are leveraging Microsoft Copilot to drive productivity for our clients.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Just as we quickly ramped a meaningful book of business around Red Hat to address the hybrid cloud opportunity, we are ahead of pace at this stage with our generative AI book of business.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Business Transformation revenue grew 3% led by supply chain and finance transformations.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Technology Consulting revenue was also up 3% with double-digit growth in cloud modernization projects, and both strategic partnerships and Red Hat engagements delivered double-digit growth.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Application Operations revenue declined, reflecting weakness in on-prem custom application management projects, partially offset by strength in cloud-based application management offerings.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Our segment profit margin was impacted by about 1 point of currency, offsetting improvements in pricing and productivity actions we have taken.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Revenue grew, reflecting growth in Hybrid Infrastructure of 6% and declines in Infrastructure Support of 7%.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Within Hybrid Infrastructure, growth was broad-based with strong demand from our hardware offerings across IBM Z, Power, and Storage.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: In IBM Z, revenue was up 5% in the eighth quarter of z16 product availability.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Now, 2 years in, this product cycle continues to resonate with clients and surpassed z15 revenue performance.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: IBM Z is uniquely positioned for AI with the first processor design with on-chip acceleration for real-time AI inferencing.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: In fact, we're working with over 100 clients on the application of AI on z16.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Use cases range from fraud detection to anti-money laundering to anomaly detection.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: This remains an enduring platform, driving not just hardware adoption but also related software, storage, and services.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Distributed Infrastructure delivered 7% revenue growth with strength in both Power and Storage.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Storage delivered strong double-digit revenue growth, including demand for high-end storage tied to the Z16 cycle.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: And clients are also looking to our storage offerings for data curation, model building, and fine-tuning and support of generative AI.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Looking at Infrastructure profit, we delivered both gross profit and segment profit margin expansion.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Segment profit margin expanded 20 basis points in the quarter, reflecting benefits from productivity while absorbing about 1 point of impact from currency.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Over this time, we've continued to invest organically and inorganically, bring new products and innovation to market, expand our ecosystem, and drive productivity across our business.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Our first-quarter performance is another proof point of this progress with constant currency revenue growth, operating gross margin and operating pretax margin expansion, and the strongest first-quarter free cash flow in many years.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Looking to the full year 2024, we are holding our view on our 2 primary metrics: revenue and free cash flow.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We see full-year constant currency revenue growth in line with our mid-single-digit model, still prudently at the low end.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: And for free cash flow, we expect to generate about $12 billion driven primarily by growth in adjusted EBITDA.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: In Software, we had a solid start to the year and continue to expect growth slightly above the high end of our mid-single-digit model.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: In Consulting, we continue to see strong demand for digital transformations.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Though, as I said, we are seeing some pressure on smaller, more discretionary projects.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We now see mid-single-digit revenue growth in Consulting with acceleration throughout the year.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Given our ongoing productivity initiatives and investment in innovation, we expect to see about 1 point of segment profit margin expansion in both of these segments.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: And in Infrastructure, given product cycle dynamics, we expect revenue to decline, driving about a 0.5 point impact to our overall growth.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Given IBM Z cycle dynamics, we expect segment profit margin to be lower year-over-year.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: With these segment dynamics, we continue to expect IBM's operating pretax margin to expand by about 0.5 point year-over-year, consistent with our view 90 days ago, and we are maintaining our view of operating tax for the year to be consistent with last year, in the mid-teens range.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We took a workforce rebalancing charge this quarter.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: On currency, given the strengthening of the dollar, we now expect a 150 to 200 basis point impact to revenue growth for the year, which is about 1 point worse than 90 days ago.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: For the second quarter, I expect our constant currency revenue growth rate to be consistent with the full year.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: And for profit, we expect the first half skew of net income will remain a couple of points ahead of the prior year.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: In closing, we are pleased with our performance to start the quarter.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We are positioned to grow revenue, expand operating profit margin, and grow free cash flow for the year.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: On demand, we continue to see and capitalize on solid demand in key areas around digital transformation, application modernization, and Gen AI.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Our signings in the quarter, up 4%, the strongest absolute first quarter signings we've had as far back as I can go.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We have a strong book-to-bill, over 1.15 on a trailing 12 months.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Our backlog dynamic is in a very strong position, 7% overall with stable erosion, but our duration has been going up the last 2 quarters.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: You talked about Gen AI.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Gen AI for IBM, Arvind indicated, inception to date, over a $1 billion book of business.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Consulting in the first quarter, the book of business on Gen AI was 2x all of last year, so I think we're winning in the marketplace.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We're taking share.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Our strategic partnerships still have great velocity, book-to-bill well north of 1.2.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: And we're seeing very nice acceleration in Gen AI and digital transformation around core workflow use case areas of finance, supply chain, HR, and talent.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We ramped on our acquisitions.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We continue to operate a very disciplined M&A process and we continue to be opportunistic, but that 2% revenue growth was all organic quarter-to-quarter.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Second, in this marketplace, you look at competition, we're taking share still.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We talked about the year was going to play out accelerating throughout the year.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Because, one, we knew we had a strong backlog and that backlog realization showed us that it was going to play out throughout the year with sequential improvement.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Two, we're continuing to focus and we are gaining share in the marketplace.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Three, we're driving that economic multiplier of consulting and technology across our hybrid cloud and AI platform.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: So in light of all that, that's why you see the mid-single-digit growth.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: I think that's prudent just given what every other consulting competitors come out with.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: By the way, that still drives 1.5 points of growth to IBM for the full year.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: And as I stated earlier, we see an accelerated growth profile as we move through the year.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: So if I look at where we are right now and where we project for the rest of the year, demand is actually quite strong.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: If I look at it by geography, Japan remains very strong.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: If you look at South Asia, extremely strong; even the Middle East, U.A.E., Saudi, very strong; Europe has remained consistent with last year; North and South America.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: So on a geography basis, we're seeing very, very strong demand.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Now interest rates are higher than people were expecting.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: One, there is even stronger demand for software and infrastructure because people believe technology helps you in those environments and helps in an environment of increased labor costs and increased supply chain costs.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Then when you look at the discretionary side, Jim answered this in the previous question, we are seeing a little bit, not across the board, not in all of the offerings in consulting, but where there is a little bit of discretionary labor, that is where we sense that pressure.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: What we are going to do is pivot into the areas around helping people become more productive, take more cost out, digital transformation, work with our partners where there is very strong demand in the market.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: And as you pivot there, we believe that our growth rate in Consulting will continue to accelerate.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: So I hope, Wamsi, that, that gave you a flavor on the demand vectors we have, both in Software and Infrastructure and in Consulting and on a geography basis.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: As Arvind indicated in the prepared remarks, we couldn't be more excited about the powerful combination of HashiCorp with IBM and Red Hat together.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We talked about it in the prepared remarks, we've been very disciplined in our set of criteria around M&A. And this fits strategically.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: It has tremendous synergistic value to our hybrid cloud and AI portfolio and it has an attractive financial return overall.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: And Hashi meets all three: One, it's a higher revenue growth profile company, so it accelerates IBM's revenue growth over time; two, to your question, adjusted EBITDA accretive in the first 12 months; and three, levered free cash flow accretive by the end of year 2.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We think there are a potential for meaningful synergies overall and, when we look at it, significant near-term operating efficiencies, cost synergies.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: And to put that in perspective, we see this business profile moving from about a mid-single-digit free cash flow margin business to about a 30% to 40% free cash flow margin business in a handful of years, free cash flow accretive by the end of year 2.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Now the multiple we paid on that, fully supported by, one, the stand-alone revenue growth and the cost synergies that come out.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: All of the IBM revenue synergies around Red Hat, around data security, around watsonx, around consulting and IT automation are all upside potential.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: So let's talk and conclude on the cost synergy.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Cost synergies are where you would fully expect.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We run a very disciplined G&A-efficient structure.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Second, running the playbook on how we expand it globally, our go-to-market model that we did with Red Hat, and that has both global incumbency, global scale, global breadth, and ecosystem leverage overall.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: And when you look at that, those significant synergies allow us to invest in product, R&D, innovation, and capability that's built into our case and also deliver our financial returns, so we feel pretty good about it.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: You look at full year, full year, as Arvind indicated, we're maintaining our guidance on our model mid-single digit, I think, prudently just coming out of a first quarter.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We've got a lot of work to do in the next 3 quarters, but I think prudently, at the low end of that model.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: When you take a look at full year, first of all, we are dealing with a stronger U.S. dollar.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: So we've given you supplemental chart, now we've lost basically about 1 point more of headwind on currency.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: When you take a look at our growth at mid-single digit, one, we said software would grow slightly above the high end of our mid-single-digit model.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We are very pleased with our Software performance in the first quarter.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We've accelerated growth from fourth quarter to 6% overall.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We have a very strong recurring revenue base.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We accelerated Red Hat to a very strong 9% with our third consecutive quarter of mid-teen booking growth, which positions our business extremely well for double-digit growth for the full year, and we're getting nice scale and leverage on acquisitions.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Software for the year will deliver over 3 points of that IBM mid-single digit by itself.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Based on that Red Hat momentum, acquisitions, solid recurring revenue; TP, by the way, nice start, up 4%; and new innovation like watsonx.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Consulting, we said for the full year, appropriately, in light of the market and still gaining share, would be mid-single digits.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: One, strong book-to-bill, winning in key focus areas, strategic partnerships, Gen AI scale overall.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: But like first quarter, we're going to continue to monitor that backlog realization to see how that plays out.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Mainframe, eighth quarter in, grew 5%.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Our Distributed Infrastructure, Power and Storage, both grew double digits as we're capitalizing on Distributed Infrastructure and demand requirements for Gen AI.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: You throw on top of that, we executed the closure of The Weather Company, that would be about 0.5 point.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: So AI book of business, I think you nailed it in your question.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: When we drove the hybrid cloud platform-centric play with Consulting, which has done extremely well, over the first 4 quarters, we did a $1 billion book of business.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We are very, very pleased with Red Hat.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: If I look at Red Hat now, we have had mid-teens or better bookings growth for the last 3 quarters, third quarter, fourth quarter, and first quarter.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: That, combined with the growth we are seeing in OpenShift as well as in both Ansible and RHEL, OpenShift growing almost 40%, gives us a lot of confidence.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: So bookings growth plus OpenShift plus what we're seeing in the revenue now at 9% tells us that we should see that Red Hat growth continue or accelerate through the year.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Hashi is a nice add for the Red Hat portfolio.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: So when we talk about Red Hat growth numbers in line and accelerating, that is Red Hat as is.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Hashi will be measured in software, but in IBM software, not in Red Hat.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Where the synergy comes is, we believe there will be added demand because if a combined portfolio is more interesting, we think even more clients will talk to us.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: That is how Hashi will help Red Hat.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: It's not that the Hashi revenue counts at all for the numbers we just mentioned.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Hashi to us is an accelerant for IBM strategy and for software strategy, and Hashi helps in being offensive in terms of giving us an overall better portfolio.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: And people know Hashi really well for their infrastructure management, but the security pieces of Hashi are also very, very interesting and really important as people navigate these very complex environments with all the worries about people losing secrets and keys and that resulting in ransomware or hacking attacks.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: As you and I and many of the investors have talked about since first quarter earnings, we've kind of bifurcated this business when we saw the slowdown happen in the second half last year between our subscription-based business within Red Hat versus our consumption-based services and offerings, the former being about 80% of our portfolio, the latter being about 20%.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: If you look at first quarter, as Arvind indicated, we're very pleased.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Coming off of a 2-plus point acceleration positions us extremely well, even more confident in that double-digit for the year.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: But the reason why we're even more confident is that 80% of that portfolio, that subscription business, we accelerated 3 points quarter-to-quarter in revenue and we were above double digits.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: But our subscription business today, the 80%, 3 points acceleration, double-digit in the first quarter, all 3 major lines broad-based double-digit bookings; Red Hat OpenShift, over 40% booking strength; $1.3 billion ARR book of business, growing 25-plus percent; Ansible taking share, we feel even more confident as I said.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We are going to remain incredibly disciplined on our M&A strategy.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We kind of said it, but I just want to repeat, we've got to find things that meet our strategy, we've got to have some synergy opportunities at IBM, and it has to be financially accretive within the second year.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: So if we find things that meet that and we are committed, I'll say, to both our dividend and our investment-grade ratings, then that is kind of the picture we go in.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: By the way, while we've got these 2 yet to come, we've got Software AG that we hope to close midyear and HashiCorp which will come near the end of the year, we also have to look at what is our overall internal dynamics of making sure that we can succeed on these businesses as we proceed down the path.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We need to have synergy plays in other parts of the portfolio.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: As we say, a big part of our synergy is getting the amplification from our global footprint that is there with clients all around the world.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: Arvind, just building on your point, we are very confident in the capital structure of this company.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: We are committed to maintain a very solid investment-grade balance sheet.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: But our primary capital allocation is to invest in our business, both organically and inorganically, and to maintain an attractive return to shareholder program with our dividend policy.

signals.speaker: James Kavanaugh
signals.sentence: So with all that said, just to reaffirm what Arvind indicated, we will remain in the market prudently evaluating complementary tuck-in opportunities that fit our M&A strategy, and we have the capability of doing that.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: But we are now seeing that we can be north of 6% for this year, whether you want to call that 6.5% or 7%, and we are very confident in that.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: As we do organic innovation and as we do M&A, we will find that, that number will keep improving year-over-year.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: By the way, within that, we do find there are a couple of slower-growing pieces, but they're incredibly important to our overall profile, both for incumbency with clients and for the cash flow that we produce.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: We would never expect our mainframe software, the TPS piece, to be growing in the high single digits or in double digits.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: And we do want to, over time, get software to grow above where we are right now.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: It's not so much directly related to VMware per se, but clients are all beginning to say, they're asking the question, which is the platform they want to bet on for the next 10 to 20 years on which they will write their applications, deploy them both in their own data centers and on public cloud.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Then as we layer in, by the end of the year, the HashiCorp advantages of managing the infrastructure across all these environments, we do believe that, that will be an accelerant to the Red Hat portfolio.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: So first, RHEL has got its place as the primary place where people want to deploy, OpenShift as a platform for both containers and virtualization, Ansible and HashiCorp helping increase automation and reduce the complexity.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: And Brian, I think the best number is the mid-teens bookings growth on the subscription side of the business.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: If we look 12 months ago, I would say that there was a lot of excitement and there was a lot of experimentation that we're starting, and people were not thinking through what does this mean for my overall ROI, what are the economics of running gen AI, how do I get the people changes done so that the ROI can actually be realized.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: Our Granite series play very strongly into helping them recognize their ROI by reducing the economics.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: And then lastly, and this is advice that I gave to the C-suite usually, and it resonates, don't take lots of little experiments, try to pick a few use cases which can scale.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: And by scale, I mean that they actually do impact a large fraction of their employees or their client's customers and they begin to have a large impact in how business is done by either improving revenue or by making the enterprise significantly more productive.

signals.speaker: Arvind Krishna
signals.sentence: That's kind of a conversation shift from simply, oh, this is a neat new tool, let me try out to see what I can do, not what I should do, but what I can do.
